section_1.title: The Binary Language (Prerequisite)
section_1.content: Introduce binary (base-2) as a system using only 0 and 1. Explain that each digit position represents a power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...). Visualize this using 'Light Switches': ON=1, OFF=0.
section_1.example: A 3-bit system: 001 (1), 010 (2), 011 (3), 100 (4). Animation: 3 switches toggling like a dance.

section_2.title: The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle
section_2.content: Define the goal: Move a stack of N disks from Peg A to Peg C, moving only one at a time and never placing a larger disk on a smaller one.
section_2.example: A monkey trying to move a 3-disk 'banana pyramid' from one tree to another following the strict rules.

section_3.title: Mapping Moves to Binary
section_3.content: Explain the surprising link: The sequence of disk moves corresponds exactly to the binary counting sequence. The number of moves required for N disks is 2^N - 1.
section_3.example: For 3 disks: 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves. Animation showing the move number (1-7) appearing as binary numbers (001 to 111) alongside the disk movement.

section_4.title: The Algorithmic Logic
section_4.content: Explain that the n-th disk moves exactly once, at step 2^(n-1). This explains why the rhythm of the puzzle is patterned—the smallest disk moves every other turn.
section_4.example: A visual 'Clock' where the small hand (disk 1) moves every tick, the middle hand (disk 2) every 2 ticks, and the large hand (disk 3) every 4 ticks.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-world Application
section_5.content: Conclude by connecting the puzzle to computer science algorithms (recursion) and data storage. Remind students that binary isn't just counting—it's the 'DNA' of logical movement.
section_5.example: Showing a computer chip or a server rack processing data packets as if they were disks in a Hanoi tower.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

        # BASE

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
